key_insight: Optimized curved rectangular vortex generators improved heat transfer or pressure-drop-aware performance in a water-to-air finned-tube heat exchanger, depending on the optimization objective.
engineering_relevance: Tailoring vortex-generator geometry can improve heat-exchanger performance while accounting for the pressure-drop penalty.
method: Developed and validated a conjugate numerical model of a representative heat-exchanger section.
Used central composite experimental design and nonlinear polynomial regression to model four geometry parameters.
Applied a genetic algorithm to optimize Colburn-factor and combined heat-transfer/friction objectives.
evidence_signal: Relative to plain fins, separate optimized configurations increased the Colburn factor by 53.1%, area goodness factor by 14.4%, and volume goodness factor by 26.5%.
watch_item: The gains belong to different optimized geometries; full-scale performance and applicability beyond the modeled conditions require verification.
paper_title: Optimization of curved vortex generator geometry for enhanced thermal performance in water-to-air finned-tube heat exchanger
